source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Limiting most forms of direct care and interaction, in the belief that this reduces unnecessary stimulation","B":"Setting aside the client's and family's expressed wishes in favor of the care team's own clinical priorities","C":"Continuing aggressive curative treatment measures despite the client's stated preference to focus on comfort","D":"Effective pain and symptom management, along with attention to psychological, spiritual, and family support needs"}}
source_row.rationale: End-of-life comfort (palliative) care prioritizes effective pain and symptom management (such as addressing dyspnea, nausea, or anxiety), along with attention to the psychological, spiritual, and emotional needs of both the client and family, focusing on dignity and quality of remaining life rather than curative intervention, in alignment with the client's and family's wishes.
source_row.source_detail: End-of-life palliative care: symptom relief plus psychosocial, spiritual, and family support; reviewed 2026-08-14.
